senses.gloss:
Bindu-mādhava
(‘Mādhava [associated with] बिन्दु’)
------------------------------------------
Taking bath in sacred rivers has been considered as a highly meritorious act since the ancient days. The गङ्गा at वाराणसी (Banaras) is one such sacred river. On the banks of this sacred river, several bathing places have been provided, with steps leading from the bank right up to the water. They are called ‘ghāṭs’.
The Pañcagaṅgā-ghāṭ is one of the five ghāṭs. Here, four rivers—Kiraṇā, सरस्वती, यमुना and Dhūtapāpā—are believed to join the गङ्गा in their subtle forms, unseen by the naked eye. Hence the name Pañcagaṅgā or five Gaṅgās or sacred rivers.
One of the temples situated at this ghāṭ is a small विष्णु temple, without the शिखर or tower. A small image of dark colour is established on a large सिṁहासन or throne. The deity is called बिन्दु-माधव.
The story goes that once Lord विष्णु visited Vārāṇāsī and sat down at the Pañcagaṅgā-ghāṭ since he liked it much. A ब्राह्मण, Agnibindu by name, who was practising severe austerities there, recognized the Lord and prayed to him with a long devotional hymn. Pleased with it, the Lord granted his wish which was twofold. The Lord had to stay there permanently and his image should be known as बिन्दु-माधव, thus perpetuating the name of the ब्राह्मण. The sacred water of the river at this ghāṭ came to be known as Bindutīrtha.

Bindusaras
(‘lake of drops of water’)
------------------------------------------
Places associated with gods or saints or saintly kings or other holy persons have been the favourite pilgrim resorts of the Hindus over the centuries. One of the less known places of पिल्ग्रिमगे is the lake बिन्दुसरस्, also known as the बिन्दु-sarovara.
The Mahābhārata (Bhīṣmaparva 6.43-46) describes a बिन्दुसरस् as situated between the mountains Maināka and Hiraṇyaśṛṅga. It is here that the king भगीरथ practised severe austerities to bring the river गङ्गा from the world of gods to the world of men. The place, even now known by the same name, is situated near Gaṅgotri (birthplace of the river गङ्गा) about 3 kms. (2 miles) to the south. A small temple dedicated to the river goddess गङ्गा stands at the place where भगीरथ is said to have practised austerities.
When the river goddess गङ्गा acceded to भगीरथ’s request to descend to this earth, शिव arrested her ferocious flow with his matted hair and then let the water out in drops which formed this बिन्दुसरस् (bindu = drop). The river गङ्गा then emerged out of this in seven streams.
The lake Kapālamocana-tīrtha at वाराणसी or काशी (modern Banaras), where शिव is said to have bathed and got rid off the sin of decapitating one of the five original heads of ब्रह्मा, is also sometimes called बिन्दुसरस्.
The Brahmapurāṇa (41.52-54) des-cribes one बिन्दुसरस् created by रुद्र (Śiva) by collecting drops of water from all the holy places and filling the lake with that. It is said to be situated in the Ekāmraka-क्षेत्र.
Two big tanks—one at Siddhapura near Ahmedabad (Gujarat) and another at भुवनेश्वर (Orissa)—also go by the same name.

bindu
(‘dot’ or ‘point’)
------------------------------------------
According to the शाक्त-तन्त्रस्, scriptures of the cult of the Divine मोथेर्, the ultimate Reality is one, a transcendental Absolute. It is immutable and ineffable. It is pictured as prakāśa, supreme effulgence. Desiring to become many, this Absolute starts reflecting on itself. This deliberation is technically designated as ‘vimarśa’. This विमर्श creates a throb or stir, स्पन्द, which develops as vibration or नाद, and gets concentrated to a point or बिन्दु. This बिन्दु, like a dicotyledonous seed, contains the शिव-शक्ति principle as one closely knit unit. It then gradually evolves into this universe.
Anusvāra, the dot placed above the letters of the Sanskrit alphabets, indicating the nasal sound, is also called ‘bindu’. It is an invariable part of the bījamantras and is said to impart an additional meaning of dispelling sorrow.
In the works on योग, बिन्दु stands for the आज्ञाचक्र, the psychic centre between the eyebrows.
See also ĀJÑĀCAKRA and NĀDA.
